Case_17005/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2a: CT of chest. Nonspecific diffuse bilateral miliary micronodular lung parenchymal process involving the visualized lower lungs.

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the chest showing diffuse bilateral miliary micronodular lung opacities.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates diffuse bilateral micronodular opacities throughout the lung parenchyma. The nodules are small and evenly distributed, consistent with a miliary pattern. The trachea and mediastinal structures appear midline, and no significant pleural effusion or lymphadenopathy is evident in this slice. The findings suggest a diffuse process, potentially infectious or granulomatous in nature.

description.short_caption: Fungal culture showing white to light brown mold growth.

Case_17005/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2b: CT of chest. Pleural-based nodular density associated with the posterior medial right lower lobe and mildly enlarged sub-carinal mediastinal lymph nodes

description.short_caption: CT chest showing pleural-based nodular density in the posterior medial right lower lobe.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest shows a pleural-based nodular density located in the posterior medial aspect of the right lower lobe. There is also evidence of mildly enlarged sub-carinal mediastinal lymph nodes. The lung parenchyma appears otherwise unremarkable, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The image is a non-contrast study, as no enhancement is noted.
